text:
A: Alright?
B: Hello.
A: Lee. I'm in Bridgwater, Somerset.
B: Shahida. Ilford.
A: Right. London, then.
B: East London. Thirty, forty years.
A: Fair enough. What d'you reckon to the puzzle?
B: It's ok. I do these for vouchers, every one has puzzle.
A: Vouchers? Didn't know that was a thing. How much you get?
B: Depends. This one is good. I save them up for my grandson's trainers. Kids' trainers, sixty pound now. Sixty.
A: Mental, innit. Everything's gone up. Parts at work, brake pads, I'm telling you, it's daylight robbery.
B: What work?
A: Mechanic. Garage, MOTs, servicing, all that.
B: My husband was minicab driver. Thirty years. He always say the garage cheating him.
A: Yeah, some of 'em do, to be fair. Half my customers come to me after some other place has had 'em over. What was he driving?
B: Toyota. Prius, at the end. Before that, Corolla. He kept it very clean, I make him.
A: Prius is a good shout for cabbing. Them things run forever. Hybrid, see, that's where it's all going now. I keep meaning to do the training.
B: So do it.
A: Yeah. Costs, though, and time. Garage won't pay for it.
B: You pay yourself, you get more money later. That's how it works.
A: Suppose. You sound like my mum.
B: Your mum is right then.
A: Ha. What d'you do, then? Before, like.
B: Shop. Ladies' suits, Green Street. Fifteen years. Stopped at sixty, my knees.
A: Knees, back, it's all the same. I done a disc four years ago. Some days I'm proper knackered just getting out the van.
B: You are young for that. You eat properly?
A: Er, yeah. Ish. Why?
B: I have diabetes. Doctor says no sugar, no sugar. Every time I go surgery, same thing.
A: Yeah, well. Doctors say a lot of things.
B: Hm. You have it also?
A: Bit, yeah. Type two. I'm sorting it. Anyway, what else you got?
B: Ok. You have children?
A: Nah. Just the dog. Diesel. He's here, look, by my leg.
B: Dog is not a child.
A: Don't tell him that.
B: Acha. I think time is finishing.
